label: Priority, basic, whole, monism and external dependence
term: priority, basic, whole, monism and external dependence
resolution: Priority monism concerns which material objects are basic, not whether parts exist, whether only one substance exists in every sense, whether the cosmos has a mind or whether God exists. Basicness excludes metaphysical dependence on concrete relata in the chosen arena, not every possible nonmaterial efficient cause. The material domain is not a closed ontology of all beings. Tiling and well-foundedness are explicit substantive commitments. A Graph.Source statement transfers only after defining a graph with edge y→x for Dxy and proving the exact structural hypotheses; the causal actualGraph and Schaffer priority relation are not silently identified. A basic composite cosmos therefore is not ruled out by mereological syntax, and its positive dependence account is not yet an intrinsic explanation of its own existence.
